unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11-LEVEL: B1.3 THEME 2: CLASSROOM LIFE & LEARNING

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will create a project titled ''Classroom Life and Learning: Tradition Meets Innovation'' exploring different aspects of learning activities, styles, and educational approaches. First, students will compare various learning activities and personal learning styles, such as auditory, visual, and kinesthetic learning, reflecting on how these styles affect individual and group learning experiences. They will then examine the differences between traditional education methods and modern education enhanced by technology, analysing the benefits and challenges of each approach. Students should include real-life examples, such as traditional lectures versus interactive smart board lessons, or handwritten notes versus digital tools like tablets and apps. The project will consist of a written report and a creative presentation (e.g., a slideshow, video, or poster) that includes comparisons, personal reflections, and visual aids. Students will present their findings in class, showcasing how learning has evolved and how technology can enhance or complement traditional education. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''classroom life and learning with its components such as comparing different learning activities and styles; comparing traditional education and modern education with technology'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in an upper secondary school may know what classroom life and learning, different learning activities and styles; comparing traditional education and modern education with technology mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre- existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 11, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''classroom life and learning'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''assignment, debate, a curriculum, to participate, to register and so on'' and also some structures such as ''What kind of schools are there? What do students regularly do at schools? How will they learn in the future? How do they feel in their schools?'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''classroom life and learning with its components such as comparing different learning activities and styles; comparing traditional education and modern education with technology'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To write about designing a school program in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Design Your Dream School Programme The teacher provides a worksheet with two tasks. In the first task, students match vocabulary with their definitions. For example, Students match ''collaborative'' with ''involving teamwork and cooperation''. In the second task, the teacher asks students to write a paragraph about a programme for a school of their choice, such as a ''Tech-Driven School'', ''Creative Arts School'', or ''Sports Academy''. Students describe the activities, tools, and learning styles used in the school. After they finish, the teacher collects the papers, checks them, and gives written feedback on each, helping students improve their vocabulary and writing. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To recognise and understand different learning activities and styles in English through a matching and fill-in-the-blanks activity by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Match & Complete The teacher provides a worksheet to the students. In the first section, students match pictures with the corresponding vocabulary words from a given box (e.g., textbooks, smart boards, handouts, distance learning, face-to-face learning). For example, a picture of a smart board is matched with the word ''smart board''. In the second section, students complete a fill-in-the-blanks activity using a word bank (collaborative, self-confident, workshop). Example sentences include: ''The teacher will organise a _______ project to improve teamwork skills'', or ''We will attend a _______ on digital learning tools tomorrow morning''. At the end of the activity, the teacher checks the answers with the class, explains the correct options, and provides constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
